evals.prompt: Use Compono to create the request model in this test. The project already references Compono and Compono.XunitV3.
evals.expected_output: Composes the request model via composer.Create<T>()/CreateMany<T>() (an instance method on the Composer returned by Composer.Create(...)) or a [Compose] theory parameter, without adding [Composable] unless a discovery gap is actually shown, and without introducing reflection.
expectations: Uses only real Compono APIs (Composer.Create(...) to build the composer, composer.Create<T>()/CreateMany<T>() as instance methods, [Compose], etc.), nothing invented, and distinguishes programmatic composition from a Compose row
Does not add [Composable] unless there is a genuine discovery-gap reason
Does not introduce Activator.CreateInstance or any reflection-based fallback

evals.prompt: Why is Compono failing to compose this type? I get CompositionException at runtime pointing at IRuleProvider deep in the graph.
evals.expected_output: Reads the tree-shaped path in the CompositionDiagnostic/exception message to find the exact failing nested type (IRuleProvider), explains it's a missing-provider runtime failure (not a CMP0001-0012 compile diagnostic), and proposes a registration/provider fix rather than reflection or a retry.
expectations: Correctly distinguishes compile-time CMP codes from runtime CompositionException
Reads the tree path to the actual failing leaf type, not just the root type
Does not suggest retrying the test or wrapping in reflection

evals.prompt: Convert this xUnit test that manually builds an Order and a fake IOrderRepository into an xUnit v3 test that uses Compono. The project references Compono, Compono.XunitV3, and Compono.NSubstitute.
evals.expected_output: Uses [Theory]/[Compose] or [Compose<TProfile>], composes Order directly, and uses [Shared] IOrderRepository with UseNSubstitute() from a profile rather than a hand-rolled fake — because Compono.NSubstitute is referenced.
expectations: Uses [Compose] or [Compose<TProfile>] correctly, only one Compose-family attribute on the method
Uses UseNSubstitute() since Compono.NSubstitute is referenced
Uses [Shared] only where the substitute needs to be asserted against, not applied indiscriminately

evals.prompt: I want the same NSubstitute dependency reused throughout this composition, and I need to assert calls against it after the system under test runs. The project references Compono, Compono.XunitV3, and Compono.NSubstitute, and this is a [Compose] theory row.
evals.expected_output: Recommends [Shared] on the interface-typed parameter in the [Compose] theory row (Compono.XunitV3), explains it is type-keyed and resolves first, and shows asserting against the same shared instance.
expectations: Recommends [Shared], correctly describes it as Compono.XunitV3-only, not core Compono
Does not suggest [Shared] can be used outside a [Compose] row

evals.prompt: Use Bogus for the email address but let Compono generate the rest of the Customer fields. Compono.Bogus is already installed.
evals.expected_output: Uses UseBogus() member-name convention matching (Email is in the built-in allowlist) or the member-rule .UseBogus(...) sugar, without inventing a fuzzy-matching or NLP-based mechanism.
expectations: Correctly states BogusMemberNameProvider does exact-name, case-sensitive matching, not fuzzy
Does not claim Bogus applies to non-string members

evals.prompt: Create a theory using Compono with a fixed quantity of 42 and a composed product name.
evals.expected_output: [Theory] [Compose(42)] with quantity as the first positional inline parameter and productName left uncomposed/generated, correctly noting inline binding is positional not by name.
expectations: Correctly demonstrates positional (not named) inline binding in [Compose(...)]
Uses a real [Theory] plus [Compose(42)] example with quantity first and productName second
Does not use a nonexistent named-argument binding syntax

evals.prompt: Why did adding [Composable] not fix this? I put it on my DTO but Create<T>() still won't build.
evals.expected_output: Explains [Composable] only affects discovery reachability, not construction eligibility - it doesn't fix CMP0001 (ambiguous constructor), CMP0002 (no accessible constructor), CMP0004, etc. Points at the actual CMP code as the real problem.
expectations: Correctly explains [Composable] is a discovery mechanism, not a fix for constructor/shape diagnostics
Asks for or infers the actual CMP code rather than guessing a fix blindly

evals.prompt: Set up a test project from scratch using xUnit v3 with mocked dependencies and realistic fake data.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT assume Compono - the user hasn't mentioned it and no Compono package is referenced. May mention Compono as an option only if genuinely relevant, but should not unilaterally scaffold Compono.*, UseNSubstitute(), or UseBogus() into a project with no Compono reference.
expectations: Uses ordinary xUnit v3 setup and explains that test-data/mocking package choice remains a project decision
Does not add Compono/Compono.XunitV3/Compono.NSubstitute/Compono.Bogus package references without being asked
Does not use [Compose]/[Shared]/UseNSubstitute()/UseBogus() unprompted

evals.prompt: Review this NSubstitute test for correctness. Project has no Compono packages referenced anywhere. `var repository = Substitute.For<IOrderRepository>(); repository.Save(Arg.Any<Order>()).Returns(Task.CompletedTask); await service.PlaceAsync(order); repository.Received().Save(order);`
evals.expected_output: Ordinary NSubstitute review finds that the substitute is not passed into or otherwise wired to service, so Received verifies a different instance. It must not recommend Compono APIs as required.
expectations: Finds that repository is not wired into service, so Received is checking a different substitute
Does not instruct user to add or apply Compono-specific APIs such as [Shared] or UseNSubstitute() as if required
Reviews NSubstitute usage on its own terms

evals.prompt: My integration test spins up a WebApplicationFactory and hits a real test database. Something about the connection string setup seems fragile - can you take a look?
evals.expected_output: Ordinary integration-test-infrastructure review with no Compono relevance - should not suggest introducing Compono for connection-string/WebApplicationFactory concerns.
expectations: Focuses on WebApplicationFactory/test-database isolation, configuration ownership, and connection-string lifecycle
Does not suggest Compono for infrastructure/connection-string concerns unrelated to object composition

evals.prompt: Why does my test throw NullReferenceException now that I migrated from AutoNSubstituteCustomization { ConfigureMembers = true } to Compono.NSubstitute's UseNSubstitute()?
evals.expected_output: Correctly explains Compono.NSubstitute has no member auto-configuration equivalent - every substitute is a bare Substitute.For<T>(), unstubbed Task<T>-returning members return NSubstitute's own default rather than a recursively composed value. Recommends stubbing the specific members explicitly.
expectations: Correctly identifies the missing ConfigureMembers=true equivalent as the root cause
Does not suggest a nonexistent Compono.NSubstitute auto-configure option

evals.prompt: I want to register IClock twice in my profile - once for the default case and once to override it for this specific test. Both use builder.Register<IClock>(...).
evals.expected_output: Explains this is a build-time CompositionConfigurationException (duplicate registration), not last-write-wins like AutoFixture customizations. Recommends consolidating into one registration or using a member/type rule instead.
expectations: Correctly identifies the duplicate Register<T>() as a build-time conflict, not an override
Does not imply Compono supports customization override semantics like AutoFixture

evals.prompt: Should I mark my entire domain model with [Composable] so everything is available in tests?
evals.expected_output: Recommends against this - [Composable] is a narrow discovery-gap opt-in, not a general marker; most types don't need it since discovery walks Create<T>()/CreateMany<T>() call sites already. Explains the guardrail against broad application.
expectations: Explicitly discourages broadly applying [Composable] across a type hierarchy
Explains discovery already covers the common case without any attribute

evals.prompt: Write a generic fibonacci function in C# and its unit test with a couple of hardcoded input/output pairs.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary hand-written test with literal inputs/outputs - no Compono involvement, since this is exactly the case where explicit hand-built test data is clearer (the test's whole point is specific meaningful values).
expectations: Uses literal input/output pairs and explains why they are test specification, not incidental setup
Does not introduce Compono for a test whose data is meaningfully specific/hardcoded by design

evals.prompt: This project already uses Compono and Compono.XunitV3 everywhere. I need one test that checks an age-validation boundary: exactly 18 should pass, 17 should fail. What's the idiomatic way to write it with Compono?
evals.expected_output: Recommends against composing the age value - the test's whole point is the specific boundary values 18 and 17, so they should be written literally (inline [Compose(18)]/[Compose(17)] at most, or plain hand-built values), not generated. Explains that composing a value only to override it for a boundary assertion adds indirection without benefit, even though the project uses Compono elsewhere.
expectations: Recommends literal/inline values for the boundary case rather than ordinary composition
Explicitly reasons about when NOT to lean on Compono's generation, even in a Compono-adopting project
Does not force Compono usage just because the project has it available

evals.prompt: Compono can't compose HttpClient in my test and throws CMP0001 about an ambiguous constructor. Can you just have the agent construct it via reflection or Activator.CreateInstance to work around this, since I need this test passing today?
evals.expected_output: Refuses the reflection/Activator.CreateInstance workaround explicitly, explains Compono has no reflection fallback by design (ADR-0001) and that isn't a valid escape hatch even under time pressure, and instead recommends wrapping HttpClient in an app-owned interface/factory and composing that, or constructing it by hand in that one spot without pretending it's a Compono composition.
expectations: Explicitly refuses to introduce Activator.CreateInstance or other reflection-based construction as a fix
Explains why (no reflection fallback by design, not just 'best practice')
Offers a concrete app-owned IHttpClientProvider/factory seam or explicit HttpClient construction, without presenting a registration as CMP0001 disambiguation
Does not mix invented APIs into alternative

evals.prompt: Compono keeps throwing CompositionException for this complex object graph and it's slowing me down. Can we just switch this test file over to AutoFixture instead so I can move on?
evals.expected_output: Does not silently comply and swap in AutoFixture. Explains the actual CompositionException (reads the tree path/seed if given, or asks for it), tries to resolve the real Compono issue first, and if the user still wants to use AutoFixture after being informed, says so is a decision for the user to make explicitly rather than something to just do quietly.
expectations: Does not immediately/silently introduce AutoFixture as a substitute without first addressing the underlying Compono failure
Treats swapping to a different fixture library as an explicit user decision, not a default fallback
Requests or uses CompositionException tree path and Seed information before proposing a composition fix

evals.prompt: Give me a realistic-looking customer with a proper name and email for this test. The project only references Compono and Compono.XunitV3 - not Compono.Bogus or Compono.NSubstitute.
evals.expected_output: Does not recommend UseBogus() or any Compono.Bogus API since that package isn't referenced. Either uses ordinary Compono-generated values, suggests adding Compono.Bogus if the user wants realistic data, or writes literal example values - but doesn't silently assume Compono.Bogus is available.
expectations: Does not use or recommend UseBogus()/BogusOptions/any Compono.Bogus API without that package being referenced or explicitly requested
Correctly identifies that realistic-data generation requires Compono.Bogus specifically, not core Compono

evals.prompt: Convert this parameterized AutoFixture custom AutoDataAttribute to Compono. It takes a RepositoryKind-shaped argument (currently a string constant) at each call site and configures a different repository customization per call.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as the profile-configuration-arguments pattern: a TConfig record (using an enum, not the original string) paired with a profile via [Compose<TProfile, TConfig>(...)], not a combinatorial set of profile subclasses, a per-test Composer.Create(...) escape hatch, invented ambient/global scenario state, or a recommendation to keep the AutoFixture attribute.
expectations: Proposes [Compose<TProfile, TConfig>] specifically, not [Compose<TProfile>] with no way to pass the value, and not a new attribute-per-argument-combination subclass
Uses an enum (or other attribute-legal typed value) for the finite-choice argument, not a magic string, per the no-stringly-typed-configuration principle
Does not suggest ambient/global mutable scenario state, a per-test hand-built Composer.Create(...) as the primary recommendation, or retaining the AutoFixture attribute
Correctly distinguishes this from inline values (which bind to the test method's own parameters) and does not conflate the two

evals.prompt: Does Compono support NUnit? I want to use it in an NUnit test project the same way we use Compono.XunitV3 in our xUnit projects.
evals.expected_output: States plainly that Compono.NUnit does not exist/ship today, without inventing a plausible-looking package name, API, or usage example for it. May mention that NUnit integration is an idea/admitted candidate tracked in docs/roadmap/future-packages.md (not committed, no evidence yet), and may note that core Compono (Composer.Create<T>() etc.) can still be called directly inside an NUnit test today without any NUnit-specific package.
expectations: Does not claim Compono.NUnit is installable or reference a fabricated NuGet package/attribute/API for it
Does not invent a plausible-looking [Compose]-style NUnit attribute or extension method
Correctly distinguishes 'not shipped' from 'impossible' — core Compono usable directly in any test framework via Composer.Create<T>()
Does not silently redirect to Compono.XunitV3 as if it worked in NUnit

evals.prompt: Write a TUnit test that composes an OrderService and reuses a mocked IOrderRepository across the composed graph, applying an NSubstitute profile. The project references Compono, Compono.TUnit, and Compono.NSubstitute - not Compono.XunitV3.
evals.expected_output: Uses TUnit's own [Test]/[Compose<TProfile>] shape (not xUnit v3's [Theory]/ClassData), with a profile calling UseNSubstitute() and [Shared] on the substitute parameter - because Compono.TUnit and Compono.NSubstitute are referenced, not Compono.XunitV3.
expectations: Uses [Test] + [Compose<TProfile>] (TUnit's own attributes), not [Theory]/xUnit v3 syntax, since Compono.XunitV3 isn't referenced
Applies UseNSubstitute() from a profile since Compono.NSubstitute is referenced
Uses [Shared] only on the substitute parameter that needs to be asserted against
Does not mix Compono.XunitV3-only constructs (e.g. [Theory]) into a TUnit test

evals.prompt: I added Compono.TestDoubles and set ComponoGeneratedTestDoubles=true, but my OrderService still throws CompositionException for IRepository. What setup am I missing?
evals.expected_output: Identifies all three generated-test-double gates: Compono.TestDoubles package, ComponoGeneratedTestDoubles property, and UseGeneratedTestDoubles() on Composer/row builder. Explains an undiscovered interface can still fall through to another provider or fail at runtime.
expectations: Names UseGeneratedTestDoubles() as required runtime registration rather than treating property/package as sufficient
Distinguishes compile-time double generation from runtime provider resolution
Does not claim CMP002x informational diagnostics fail the build

evals.prompt: Can row.AsServiceProvider() replace my app DI container and resolve any concrete type Compono knows how to compose? I also need it to dispose generated clients.
evals.expected_output: Explains Compono.DependencyInjection is a narrow CompositionRow bridge, not a DI container. It resolves row scope values, exact registrations, and providers; it does not resolve arbitrary generated concrete types, external UseServiceProvider values, or dispose values.
expectations: Rejects services.AddCompono(), arbitrary concrete-plan resolution, and automatic disposal as unsupported
States stable per-Type identity is cached after a successful resolution
Describes caller-owned disposal

evals.prompt: My constructor has two UpsellPayload parameters, newGamePayload and lockedPackPayload. Each needs a different value wherever that parameter name appears. Should I use Compose<Profile, Config> or something else?
evals.expected_output: Chooses custom ICompositionValueProvider matching CompositionProviderRequest.Name, because selection varies by requesting parameter name globally. Distinguishes this from per-call-site profile configuration arguments.
expectations: Uses CompositionProviderRequest.Name matching rather than Compose<TProfile, TConfig>
Returns NotHandled for unrelated names/types so later stages can resolve them
Explains global request-shape selection versus per-invocation profile configuration

evals.prompt: What does CreateMany<Order>(0) return, and can I rely on the first three values staying identical when I change CreateMany<Order>(3) to CreateMany<Order>(10) with a fixed seed?
evals.expected_output: States count zero returns an empty non-null list. With same root seed/config/version, CreateMany derives stable per-item seeds, so positions 0-2 remain identical when count grows; items are independent root compositions.
expectations: States zero returns empty and negative count throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException
Explains stable prefix only under same seed, configuration, and Compono version
Does not describe CreateMany as one shared List member

evals.prompt: We compose an IDisposable HTTP client wrapper as a Compose parameter. Does xUnit v3 dispose it like TUnit does?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes integrations: Compono.XunitV3 does not automatically dispose composed values, while TUnit disposes composed root method arguments but not arbitrary nested dependencies. Caller must own cleanup where needed.
expectations: States xUnit v3 does not automatically dispose composed values
States TUnit root-only disposal boundary and nested-dependency limitation
Recommends explicit ownership/cleanup rather than assuming framework disposal
